clue.text: Check off merchandise, seconds gone — time sensed passing?

parts.note: to tick is to check off an item on a list

indicators.note: gone says the letter for seconds has been taken away from the goods word

parts.note: stock is goods held for sale

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper checks off goods against a clock, feeling the seconds drift away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes S from STOCK, leaving TOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of a clock is what you hear as the seconds and minutes go by, so it is time made audible.

clue.text: Opening of Bolero in short stressed beats

indicators.note: in places the first letter of the dance title inside the shortened word
short says the word for turmoil is cut down by a letter

parts.note: someone stressed is in the throes, in turmoil

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musician describes the insistent pounding rhythm that opens Ravel's Bolero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops an E from THROES to give THROS, and 'in' puts B within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulsing beats, as of a heart or a drum, are synonyms of the plural noun.

clue.text: Clothes designer more comfortable holding in stomach

indicators.note: holding in says the word for comfier keeps the belly word inside it

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more comfortable
tum is an informal word for the stomach

explanation.surface: A fashion designer, now more at ease, still sucks in their belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, a designer and maker of theatrical clothing.

clue.text: Concede when low, with three not out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket side, struggling at three wickets down, gives up the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'not out' is still in; here 'out' is the anagram signal. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a boxer's corner signalling surrender, means to admit defeat or give up.

clue.text: In extremes of cowardice, trying to defend a pretence

indicators.note: In says that whole assembly sits within the outer letters of the cowardice word
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
to defend is to surround and protect, so the difficult word encloses the letter A

parts.note: hard means difficult, trying

explanation.surface: A coward tries to keep up a false show of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence or empty show put on to deceive.

clue.text: Last of balls brown, setter potted — some plant!

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word
potted means sunk into, so the setter word is put inside the brown word

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A snooker player sinks the final brown ball, setting up a pun on a potted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing organ of a flower, so it is some part of a plant.

clue.text: Bully got shirty about me, fine young adult!

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the other two pieces
to bully is to push around, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: fine means thin, as of a thread

explanation.surface: A bully loses temper at the speaker, and someone remarks on the young person's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of GOT SHIRTY splits round METHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in their thirties is a fairly young adult, the label coming from a TV drama.

clue.text: Joint that goes to a bishop's head!

definitions.meaning: a carpentry join at an angle, as at the corner of a picture frame

definitions.text: that goes to a bishop's head
definitions.meaning: a bishop's tall pointed ceremonial hat

explanation.surface: A wry quip about what goes to a cleric's head, like drink or vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an angled woodworking joint and a bishop's tall headdress.

clue.text: Old money invested in particular drug

indicators.note: invested in says the money pieces are put inside the fussy word, like cash put into a fund

parts.note: nice can mean particular, fussy, precise
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: An investor puts old money into a specific drug company.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the addictive stimulant found in tobacco, a drug.

clue.text: Defensive cover thrown around legionary's head

indicators.note: around says the throwing word wraps the picked letter

parts.note: shied means thrown, as a stone at a target

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier's protection is hurled about in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is held up to protect the body, a defensive cover.

clue.text: Part of a step in error is eradicated

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a mistake in a step has been corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase the vertical face between treads is called the riser.

clue.text: In Greek, man is lacking belief

indicators.note: In says the man and is pieces go inside the Greek word

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: In ancient Greece, some man has lost his faith in the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheistic describes someone who does not believe in any god, lacking religious faith.

clue.text: Giant teary, cry audibly

parts.note: teary means sad, low, blue

indicators.note: audibly says the crying word is heard, giving a sea creature that sounds the same

parts.note: to wail is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: A huge figure, tearful, sobs out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest animal ever known is a giant of the ocean, so a giant serves as its description.

clue.text: River Test's first opening

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening in fabric

explanation.surface: A river named Test has an opening at its source.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test and the Trent are both English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Steering mechanism inspiring a church, as intended

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the steering word takes the letter A inside it

parts.note: a fin steers a fish or a boat
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A steering system breathes life into a church, just as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a betrothed partner.

clue.text: Brown boxes thrown past waste collector

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the colour word holds the other piece

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed into disorder

explanation.surface: Brown containers are hurled past a binman.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat scoop into which dirt is swept, it gathers household rubbish.

clue.text: Colour in jogging top due to change in cost

indicators.note: in says the reordered letters go inside the cost word

parts.note: price means cost

indicators.note: to change says these letters are reordered
top picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A jogger's top colour has to change because of its cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour' looks like a noun but is the verb, to bias; 'to change' scrambles the jogging initial with DUE to give EJUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour a judgement is to bias or prejudice it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Light head in mountain climbing, relative indication something amiss?

indicators.note: in says the picked letter goes inside the reversed heap
climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a pile is a heap or mountain

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A light shines at a mountain summit while a relative climbs, hinting something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PILE into ELIP; 'in' places L inside it to give ELLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots in text signal that words are missing, so they indicate something left out.

clue.text: Dog initially can't hear piercing siren?

indicators.note: piercing says the initials go through the middle of the temptress word

parts.note: a siren is a temptress, one who lures

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A dog at first cannot hear a shrill alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, typically greyhound with collie or terrier.

clue.text: On TV channel, live!

parts.note: re means on or concerning
side is dated British slang for a television channel, as in 'switch to the other side'

explanation.surface: An announcer declares a TV programme is being broadcast live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' reads as a broadcast term but is the verb to dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to have one's home somewhere, to live there.

clue.text: Top steeplechaser, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a knitted garment worn on the upper body, a sweater
a horse that leaps fences in a steeplechase

explanation.surface: Praise for the best horse in a steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a knitted pullover is called by this name, and a horse racing over fences is one too.

clue.text: White ball to sink for the biggest prize

parts.note: in bowls the jack is the small white target ball
to pot a ball is to sink it into a pocket

explanation.surface: Sinking the white ball wins the top award.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or gambling game.

clue.text: Lie, one covered up by principals in approved school already

indicators.note: covered by means the initials sit on top, before the reversed piece
principals are the first letters of the words
up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: how a thing lies is how it sits
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lie was covered up by the heads of an approved school already.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the lie and one to give ITIS, and 'covered by' sets the initials above it. An approved school was a former British reform school for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of affairs, things being so already.

clue.text: Brick I picked up on back of van

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: got means picked up, obtained

explanation.surface: A worker lifts a brick onto the rear of a van.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a brick-shaped block of cast metal, especially gold.

clue.text: Tipple in the main thrown up, ultimate in crude stuff

indicators.note: thrown up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: grog is rum and water, the drink served at sea, the main being the ocean

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor's drink is vomited up, a crude business.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself with food, a verb sense.

clue.text: Sharp tool caught in posterior, sure painful

indicators.note: in says the cricket letter goes inside the backside word

parts.note: seat is a polite word for the backside
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: painful suggests a sore twist, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp tool lodged in someone's backside is surely painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are sharp pruning shears used by gardeners, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Pseud out to impress team, failed miserably

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the team word goes inside the rearranged letters
out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A pretentious type sets out to impress a team and flops.
explanation.definitionFit: To have botched something badly is informal for having failed miserably.

clue.text: Clown Grimaldi used gladioli to squirt every one at the back

indicators.note: every one at the back picks the last letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: The famous clown Joseph Grimaldi used flowers to squirt water at people.
explanation.definitionFit: Clown can mean a foolish person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Tough swimmer in dirty hole

indicators.note: in says the swimmer sits inside the filthy place

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, a pigsty
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: A hardy fish survives in a filthy hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and determined, like steel, so tough.

clue.text: Disease in animals causes amazement

definitions.meaning: a disorder of horses and sheep causing a reeling gait

explanation.surface: A sickness among livestock that shocks onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a livestock illness, and the verb means astonishes.
